q1.position: Clone the OBSERVABLE contract by running Electron's main-process state machines in the Bun facade over host-owned primitives; never clone Electron's authority topology. Concretely: (1) `@keld/electron` (TS, over `@keld/api`) owns every Electron-shaped object, its EventEmitter ordering, its destroyed-tombstone, and the Electron lifecycle sequencing (close→beforeunload→unload→closed; destroy skips close but guarantees closed; app.quit → per-window close → before-quit → will-quit → quit; quitAndInstall inverts before-quit/close). The host emits only primitive, generation-tagged events (WindowCloseRequested, WindowDestroyed, LastWindowClosed, NavigationCommitted) and the facade orders the Electron-visible emissions. Electron's ordering is a browser-process JS ordering, not an OS ordering, so this is where it belongs. (2) `keld-compat` (Rust) owns only what JS cannot fake and what mints authority: webview routing identity (`webContents.send` → host-routed EVENT to one webview principal; `event.sender`/`senderFrame.url` minted by host), window parenting/modals, custom-scheme declaration with explicit privilege bits, cookie/proxy subset, nativeImage codecs. (3) The renderer compat user-script runs the app's preload file in the isolated WKContentWorld at document start with a `require` shim exposing exactly the sandboxed-preload module map (`electron`={ipcRenderer, contextBridge, webFrame subset}, events, timers, url); `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` installs a proxy in the page world that talks to the isolated world over the KEL-142 page↔isolated handoff; functions proxied, prototypes dropped, Promise returns supported — the same table Electron documents. (4) Sync getters: the facade keeps a host-pushed shadow mirror (bounds, focus, isDestroyed, displays, shouldUseDarkColors, getAllWindows) ordered on the same per-channel stream as events, so `isDestroyed()` after `closed` is deterministically true and sync reads cost zero round trips; a getter whose freshness is semantically required (dialog.show*Sync, nativeTheme at startup) is a BLOCKING kipc CALL from Bun with a deadline — Bun's client is already a blocking reader (`echo_call`), and 02 §5/KEL-127 explicitly sanction a blocking CALL. User-interaction calls (modal dialogs) carry no application deadline; the host suspends inbound host→Bun CALL deadlines while Bun is parked in a modal CALL and queues them (otherwise Cmd+Q with two dirty windows times out — see Q4). (5) Renderer `sendSync`: the only honest implementation is a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned (02 §5, KEL-127); on WKWebView that means a synchronous XHR to a host-owned scheme that the host forwards to Bun [inference — unverified engine behavior, see Q4 experiment]. A deadline expiry throws a typed `KELD-IPC-*` error where Electron would hang forever: scoreboard ▲, not silent. draw.io has zero sendSync sites; Zettlr has 6 in preload/pinia — so it is NOT on the first-proof path. (6) Destroyed objects: every facade object is a (handle, generation) pair; after the host's Destroyed event the facade tombstones it and all methods/property reads throw `Object has been destroyed` synchronously, matching the documented text. The race window (host destroyed, Bun not yet drained) is bounded by the event queue; a call that reaches the host for a dead handle comes back `KELD-*` and the facade re-throws the Electron text on the Promise path. Record the race as ▲ with its exact description. (7) Divergence routing rule (already set by KEL-72 and I would keep it): host/kipc constraints that no app can toggle → scoreboard ▲ with conformance test (app.quit Promise<void>, per-listener try/catch, sendSync deadline, close-veto deadline); per-app behavioral toggles with two defensible behaviors → `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag (windowOpenHandler strictness, accelerator edge cases, `webRequest` file:// filter → navigation allow-list); documented-never → ✘ with the published list. A quirks flag may never widen authority; if a flag would, it is a guard manifest grant instead. (8) Oracle: Electron's documented behavior plus Keld-owned tests citing exact Electron test identities and immutable blobs (research 214); never run Electron's `spec/` under Bun.

q2.position: MEASURED today (narrow, diagnostic, Windows-heavy): host/main-process RSS 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (Windows direct-COM session; Electron won TOTAL process-tree RSS in the broader Windows runs); host executable 484,864 B vs Tauri 8,634,880 B; Windows kipc Bun↔Rust p99 ≈101.6 µs fresh / 100.5 µs warm (1 session, 10k calls, 25-byte payload — publication.eligible=false); host-only first paint KELD 469 ms vs Electron 275 ms vs Tauri 479 ms (Electron leads); macOS WK host-only paint median 342.9 ms; Bun extension-host bootstrap PoC 53% sooner to Initialized. TARGETS (01 §5): ≤20 MB/≤6 MB installer, ≤300 ms paint, ≤90 MiB idle RSS (host+guardian+Bun), ≤100 µs kipc p99, ≤50 KB patch, ≤2 s keld dev. PROJECTIONS (allowed only labelled): 75–87% smaller package IF ≤20 MB is met. Where the advantage actually comes from: not bundling Chromium (bytes), a GC-free host that owns windows (host RSS, idle wakeups), Bun's startup (role boot), a binary typed frame (control-plane latency), and content-addressed updates (patch bytes). Where COMPATIBILITY COSTS performance, by mechanism: (a) hop count — draw.io's `ipcRenderer.send('rendererReq') → ipcMain.on → event.reply('mainResp') → ipcRenderer.on` is 2 hops in Electron (renderer↔browser) but 4 in Keld (webview→host→Bun→host→webview) with two SCV encode/decode pairs and, on WKWebView, a native→page delivery that is a JS evaluation into the isolated world (string serialization) — this is the term most likely to be ms-class, and it has never been measured; (b) `webContents.send` fan-out — same per-message JS-eval cost; Zettlr has 49 call sites, draw.io 15; (c) sync emulation — every blocking CALL parks the Bun event loop; a shadow mirror makes getters free but adds a steady-state event stream (allocation pressure on the hot path must stay zero per AGENTS); (d) close-veto round trip — every window close becomes a host→Bun CALL→REPLY before the OS window may close; (e) structured-clone codec — postcard SCV for Buffer/Date/Map/Set/Error, bulk-lane refs for TypedArrays: correct but not free, and JSON-only in slice 1; (f) preload bridge — `contextBridge` proxies cross the page↔isolated-world handoff, a per-call DOM-event or message hop that Electron does in-process via V8 context switching; (g) menu/dialog/clipboard brokers — each native call is a kipc CALL plus guard evaluation vs. Electron's in-process call. The advantage is architectural (bytes, host RSS, patches); the cost is per-message and per-call. Whether the net is positive for an IPC-chatty editor is UNKNOWN and must be measured on draw.io itself, with the same app on Electron on the same Mac.

q3.position: The fastest HONEST path to 'draw.io Desktop config-only on macOS' is to run the first proof under the explicitly labelled `legacy` authority profile, keep the Electron facade strictly on the already-approved spine substrate (KEL-142's isolated-world bridge, KEL-72's lifecycle session, KEL-74's evidence schema, KEL-237's lifecycle corpus), and score only `install` + `activation` + a 4-step `primary_workflow` (open → edit → save → close-with-unsaved-prompt). Rationale: draw.io's 4.5k-line main is ordinary Node (fs, path, url, child_process spawn/execFile, electron-store, electron-log, electron-updater); a strict-profile Bun role has zero ambient OS authority and keld-native brokers only fs.read/fs.write today, so a strict-profile config-only run would require a `node:fs`→broker shim plus `child_process`→role mapping — a spec of its own and not on the spine. Legacy profile is a sanctioned Keld state (03 §2) as long as the evidence record carries `authority_profile: legacy` and the scoreboard says so; promoting draw.io to strict is a later cell, not a precondition. Sequence relative to the spine: KEL-140 (one guarded fs op) and KEL-143 (recovery) do not block the Electron proof's lanes B/C/D below; they block the strict-profile cell. KEL-141 (prebuilt mac CLI) gates the final 'config-only from a clean checkout' artifact because `keld migrate` and `keld build` are KELD-CLI-045 reserved today. Do NOT reorder #312: the KELD-native vertical slice (KEL-139 tasks) stays first; the compat lanes run beside it on disjoint crates and consume its artifacts.

Run the app's preload file in the isolated WKContentWorld at document start with a `require` shim exposing the sandboxed-preload module map; `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` → page-world proxy with Electron's type table (functions proxied, prototypes dropped, Promise ok, Symbol throws); `ipcRenderer.send/on/once` ⇄ `ipcMain.on/once` with `event.reply`, `event.sender.send`, `event.senderFrame.url` (host-minted, null after navigation), `webContents.send`, `process.type`/`process.versions` in preload; codec = JSON-cloneable subset (▲ for Buffer/Date/Map/Set until SCV lands). Gating: draw.io's electron-preload.js loads unmodified and `request()`→`rendererReq`→`mainResp` round-trips; conformance: per-channel ordering under 10k messages, Function argument throws, senderFrame null after navigation, exposeInMainWorld of full ipcRenderer yields empty object; first renderer-inclusive RTT diagnostic (Q2) recorded as diagnostic, not score.

S3 — Guarded native brokers that draw.io's primary workflow touches (crates/keld-native one broker per concern, keld-guard ops, @keld/electron facades): `dialog.showOpenDialog/showSaveDialog/showMessageBox` + `showMessageBoxSync` as a blocking CALL with no application deadline and host-side deadline suspension; `shell.openExternal` with a host scheme/host allow-list (never a raw dispatch); `Menu.setApplicationMenu`/`buildFromTemplate` (AppKit main menu, roles, accelerators); `screen.getAllDisplays/getPrimaryDisplay`, `nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors`, `app.getPath/getLocale/getVersion/getName`, `clipboard` read/write text/image subset, `nativeImage.createFromPath` for the window icon, `webContents.executeJavaScript`, `zoomFactor`/`setVisualZoomLevelLimits`, `before-input-event`. Writes `keld.config.ts`, `keld.permissions.jsonc` (seeded from static analysis of Electron API usage per 03 §3), `keld.compat.ts` (quirks: `webRequestFileFilter→navigationAllowList`, `windowOpenHandler: strict`), `tsconfig.json` paths alias `electron`→`@keld/electron` (bunfig alias does NOT remap runtime import on Bun 1.3.x), and aliases `electron-updater`→`@keld/electron` autoUpdater-shaped adapter that emits the event names draw.io subscribes to and turns `setFeedURL` into a scored diagnostic (feed stays host-declared); `electron-store`/`electron-log`/`electron-context-menu` load as-is under legacy (context-menu scored ✘ for now, outside the denominator). Commit `keld.compat.denominator/v1` for `panel: product`, `corpus_id: drawio-desktop`, kinds `install`, `activation`, `primary_workflow` (open/edit/save/close-with-prompt), document the committed product corpus id so `score` may emit `unweighted_percent`; CI runs the harness per cell with negative controls and no retries (214); regenerate compat-scoreboard.md from evidence. q4.kill_risk: Synchronous-veto and blocking-call semantics across the host↔Bun boundary. Electron's whole lifecycle contract assumes the browser process IS the JS main: `close` is vetoed synchronously by `event.preventDefault()`, `dialog.showMessageBoxSync` blocks the main while the OS still pumps, `isDestroyed()` is a same-process read, and `app.quit()` serially closes every window while the app's handlers run inside those closes. Keld puts a process boundary, a deadline, and a default-deny guard between each of those. draw.io's close dance (close → preventDefault → async renderer `isModified` → `showMessageBoxSync` → `saveAndClose` round trip → `destroy()` → `closed`) is the canonical editor pattern; every corpus editor (Zettlr too) has it. If the host cannot hold a WindowCloseRequested open while Bun is parked inside a blocking modal CALL — and still accept a second WindowCloseRequested for another dirty window during Cmd+Q — without deadlock, deadline expiry, or closing the window anyway (data loss), then no config-only editor migration is possible, and the only fixes (host-side ownership of the decision, or app rewrites to async two-phase close) either violate the four uniques or break 'config-only'. I rank this above WKWebView Service-Worker-on-custom-scheme (real, CANNOT, but irrelevant to draw.io which loads file:// and disables webviews — it kills Zettlr-class/VS Code-class later, not the program), above native addons (draw.io has none), above Bun Node-compat gaps (bounded, package-by-package, legacy profile absorbs most), and above event-ordering fidelity in general (ordering lives in the facade and is testable in isolation; the veto is the one ordering that needs the host to WAIT).

q1.position: Clone Electron's observable contract at exactly three seams and refuse to let any of them become an authority seam. (1) TS facade `@keld/electron` over `@keld/api`: every Electron module/class is a thin state machine holding a host-minted (id, generation) handle, never an OS handle; all mutation is a typed CALL, all observation is either an ordered host EVENT mirror or a CALL. (2) Host-side emulation in `keld-compat` (Rust, behind `keld-guard`): things JS cannot fake and that mint authority if faked in JS — `protocol`/resource transport, `session` subset (CSP injection, file:// containment, webRequest subset), `webContents` routing identity (`event.sender`/`senderFrame` minted by host), window parenting/modals, nativeImage codecs, single-instance admission with typed argv. (3) Renderer compat user-script installed in a non-page WKContentWorld (KEL-142 seam) implementing `ipcRenderer`, `contextBridge`, `webFrame` subset, `process.argv`/`additionalArguments`, and a sandboxed-preload `require('electron')` polyfill over `window.keld.{invoke,send,on}`. Synchronous surfaces are handled honestly in two different ways: main-process sync getters (`isMaximized`, `getFocusedWindow`, `app.getPath`) read a host-pushed, per-window ordered state mirror (one lifecycle/window EVENT channel, FIFO), documented ▲ 'mirror may lag one event'; `app.getPath` is a static table sent at `Ready` (✔). Renderer `sendSync` stays what KEL-127 ordered: a blocking CALL with a deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned, surfaced as a throw with a `KELD-COMPAT-*` code on deadline; the only engine-portable renderer-blocking primitive is a synchronous XHR to the host scheme handler, whose feasibility on WKWebView is [unknown] and must be the first experiment; until it passes, `sendSync` is ✘ with a fix-it, never a hidden async rewrite. Destroyed-object semantics: the host owns the window generation; the facade tombstones on the host `closed` EVENT and every later method/property access throws `Object has been destroyed` (Electron's documented text); `destroy()` skips `close`/`beforeunload` but guarantees `closed`; `close` is cancellable via `preventDefault` round-tripped as a CALL reply before the host proceeds. Event ordering is reproduced by putting all window-lifecycle and app-lifecycle events for all windows on one ordered channel per link (kipc guarantees per-channel ordering), so `close -> closed -> window-all-closed`, `before-quit -> windows close -> will-quit -> quit` are host-sequenced, and conformance tests assert the sequence, not just emission. Divergences: a host/kipc constraint that cannot be toggled per app is a scoreboard ▲ (e.g. `app.quit(): Promise<void>`, per-listener try/catch isolation); a per-app behavior preference is a `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag (windowOpenHandler strictness, CSP merge policy, updater disabled); anything on the never list or not yet owned is ✘ with the tracking id. A quirks flag can narrow behavior, never widen authority; `keld.compat.ts` is not a permission file and the guard never reads it. What must never be emulated is below.

Ship the `remote` module, full CDP in production webviews, or a second manifest/permission parser inside the facade.
Hide a divergence: every behavior that differs is a ▲ row, a quirks flag, or a ✘; prose in a README is not a divergence record.

q2.position: Keld's advantage is structural, not linguistic: no bundled Chromium (installer and process baseline), a small Rust host instead of a Node main, and Bun for Node-shaped work. Every one of those is measured only narrowly today and two headline rows currently go the other way (Windows host-only first paint 469 ms vs Electron 275 ms; Electron's smaller process tree won total RSS on Windows). Compatibility costs performance in four specific places and each must be attributed before any 'faster IPC' or 'lower memory' sentence is written for migrated apps: (a) facade round trips — Electron's renderer->main invoke is one Mojo hop with in-process dispatch, Keld's is renderer -> WKScriptMessageHandler -> host router (+guard) -> app-link -> Bun and back, i.e. two hops, two codec passes and one guard evaluation per call; (b) SCV codec — the postcard structured-clone sum type must encode Date/Map/Set/Error/TypedArray; TypedArray is a bulk-lane ref, which on wv-link is a custom-scheme request, not shared memory; (c) sync emulation — a blocking renderer `sendSync` via synchronous XHR stalls the WebContent main thread for the full two-hop RTT plus scheme-handler overhead, and every `isMaximized`-class getter served by a mirror adds an EVENT per state change; (d) chatty `webContents.send` — Zettlr has 84 send sites and 49 webContents.send sites, draw.io 15; each is a host-routed EVENT with a per-frame guard check. Separate the three claim classes strictly: MEASURED — Windows main-process RSS 19,552 KB vs 89,140 KB (host-only, Electron total tree lower); Windows kipc Bun<->Rust diagnostic p50 47.6/p99 101.6 µs fresh, 100.5 µs warm (not publication-eligible); macOS untraced first-paint proxy 342.911 ms and Windows 469 ms host-only arms; Windows paired `keld dev` host 22.3 MiB vs Tauri 26.2 MiB; VS Code ext-host bootstrap under Bun 53.3% sooner to Initialized in a 30-run PoC. TARGET — the architecture 01 §5 table (≤20 MB/≤6 MB installer, ≤300 ms paint, ≤90 MiB idle RSS, ≤100 µs p99, ≤50 KB patch, ≤2 s dev). PROJECTION — 75-87% smaller package and 70-90% lower cold start are arithmetic on targets against a survey baseline and may be used only with that label. q4.kill_risk: The authority-model collision: 'config-only migration' versus 'zero ambient OS authority in Bun'. A median Electron main process — draw.io included — performs raw `node:fs` reads/writes on renderer-supplied paths, and its ecosystem packages (electron-store, electron-log, electron-updater) hard-wire `fs`, `net` and process spawning. Keld's strict profile (KEL-78) denies that ambient authority at the OS level, has no `node:fs`-over-broker compat facade, and its macOS mechanism is unverified; KEL-78 also states that a JS shim cannot mediate native code. If the only profile under which draw.io runs config-only is `legacy`, then every migrated app ships with Electron-equivalent main-process authority, the differentiator that justifies the architecture is absent from the product's headline use case, and the pressure to make `legacy` the de-facto default (a silent downgrade, which KEL-127 and architecture 03 forbid) becomes the program's failure mode. Runners-up that would kill a specific corpus app rather than the program: (i) `sendSync` has no renderer-blocking primitive on WKWebView (kills Zettlr config load; draw.io unaffected); (ii) `file://` URL identity — if the host serves app files under `keld://`, draw.io's `validateSender` (`frame.url.startsWith(codeUrl)`) rejects every IPC message, so the host must present real `file://` origins with native read-access containment; (iii) WKWebView Service Workers on custom schemes (WebKit 206741, status NEW) — irrelevant to file://-loaded draw.io, relevant to any app that relies on `protocol.handle` + `allowServiceWorkers`.

Pass criterion: 100% of activation + primary_workflow rows are scopable and zero rows are spawn/dlopen — then a strict path exists (OS sandbox from KEL-78 as the boundary + a `node:fs` compat facade routed to the KEL-130 broker as convenience, with dialog-minted scopes) and the first proof may be scheduled for `strict` as a second cell. q1.position:
Clone the observable contract, not the machine. Keld reproduces Electron's API + semantics + lifecycle + events + errors + defaults in exactly four places, each with one owner, and refuses anything that would move authority or a UI-thread block across a boundary.

WHERE EACH LAYER LIVES
1. Module alias (migrate-owned): `electron` -> `@keld/electron` via `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions.paths`; `bunfig.toml [alias]` is written for the named-file contract but is NOT the runtime resolver (arch 04 §3 v0 note) [fact]. I ran the scratchpad alias probe on Bun 1.4.2: the tsconfig paths alias remaps `import {app} from "electron"` in app code AND inside a node_modules dependency to the shim [fact]. That means draw.io's electron-store/electron-log/electron-updater/electron-context-menu resolve to the facade without patching them; this must become a conformance test, not an assumption.
2. Main-process facade (`@keld/electron`, TS only, consumer of `@keld/api`): BrowserWindow/ipcMain/dialog/Menu/etc. are TS classes over typed `@keld/api` channels; the direct lifecycle transport must not be duplicated in both packages (KEL-142 §4.3) [fact]. The facade owns Electron-shaped *semantics* (EventEmitter surface, tombstones, error strings, defaults) and nothing privileged.
3. Renderer compat user-script (`ipcRenderer`/`contextBridge`/`webFrame` subset): installed in the non-page `WKContentWorld` by `keld-wv` (`macos_bridge.rs` uses `defaultClientWorld` + `addScriptMessageHandler_contentWorld_name`; page-world fallback is forbidden) [fact]. `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` = frozen object projected into pageWorld; preload runs in the isolated world before page scripts, and `process.argv` must carry `webPreferences.additionalArguments` because draw.io's preload reads `--initial-adaptive-colors=` from `process.argv` [fact].
4. Host-side emulation (`keld-compat` Rust + brokers): only things JS cannot fake — webContents routing identity (host mints principal ids), window parenting/modals, custom scheme/resource transport, session subset, nativeImage codecs (arch 04 §3 item 4) [fact]. No Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc.

SYNCHRONOUS GETTERS AND sendSync, HONESTLY
- Main-process sync getters (draw.io calls `win.getSize()/getPosition()/isMaximized()/isFullScreen()` inside its `close` handler and `BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()` x6 [fact]): window state lives in the host, so a getter is either a shadow read or a blocking RTT. Rule: any getter with a defining host event (bounds/move/maximize/focus/fullscreen/closed) reads a host-pushed shadow updated on the ordered lifecycle stream — zero RTT, no allocation — and is recorded ▲ ("reflects last host-delivered state"). Getters/ops with no defining event (`dialog.showMessageBoxSync`, which Electron documents as blocking the process [fact]) use a real block: Bun main thread `Atomics.wait` on a SharedArrayBuffer while a worker runs the kipc CALL. I ran the probe: Bun 1.4.2 main-thread `Atomics.wait` returns `ok` on worker notify (61 ms for a 50 ms timer) [fact]. The block carries a deadline (Electron blocks forever; Keld bounded = ▲), is rate-limited, dev-warned, and policy lives in `keld.compat.ts` `sendSync policy` (arch 04 §2) [fact].
- Renderer `ipcRenderer.sendSync`: page JS in WKWebView cannot block on `postMessage`. Candidate mechanisms are a synchronous XHR against the `keld://` scheme handler or a `WKUIDelegate` prompt hijack; whether either is safe on the UI-process main thread is [unknown] until a discriminating experiment runs. draw.io uses sendSync 0 times; Zettlr uses it 6 times (`config-provider`, `citeproc-provider`) [fact]. Therefore: `sendSync` is `SCAFFOLDED` for the draw.io proof (throws a typed `KELD-*` with migration guidance), and the real mechanism is a Zettlr-gated slice. Shipping a fake-async `sendSync` is forbidden (KEL-127: it changes the caller contract).

DESTROYED OBJECTS AND EVENT ORDERING
- Electron: `close` (cancelable via preventDefault, before DOM beforeunload/unload) -> `closed`; `destroy()` skips `close`/unload but guarantees `closed`; property access after destroy throws `Object has been destroyed` [fact, browser-window.md@v44.4.5]. Keld: each facade object holds a generation + local tombstone flipped by the host `closed`/`destroyed` event; every method checks the tombstone synchronously and throws the exact Electron message with no round trip; a call that races the event and reaches the host for a stale generation gets a stale-generation `KELD-*` which the facade maps to the same `Object has been destroyed` throw/rejection (▲: the race window exists in Keld, not Electron). `isDestroyed()` reads the tombstone.
- Cancelable `close`: the host must not block its UI thread on Bun (KEL-142 §6) [fact], so `close` is a host->Bun CALL with a deadline; the window stays open until the reply; on deadline expiry the host proceeds and records ▲ (Electron would hang on a stuck main).
- Ordering: one FIFO per principal on one kipc link; per-channel ordering is the contract (arch 02 §5) [fact]; cross-window ordering is host-sequenced. Per-listener try/catch in `emit` is already a recorded ▲ (listener isolation vs EventEmitter propagation) [fact]. Every slice lands a sequence test (`close->closed`, `destroy->closed only`, `ready->window-all-closed->before-quit->will-quit->quit`) before implementation (keld-compat AGENTS) [fact].
- Errors: `ipcMain.handle` throws deliver only `message` to the renderer [fact, ipc-main.md]. Keld matches "message only" and must not leak stacks/endpoint/token (KEL-142 §7) — this is the one place Electron's loss of fidelity is also Keld's security requirement.

SURFACING DIVERGENCE (one rule)
- `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag = a per-app behavioral toggle the migrator may legitimately choose (e.g., `session.webRequest.onHeadersReceived/onBeforeRequest` on draw.io become no-ops because the host already injects CSP and owns the resource scheme; `will-attach-webview` no-op because draw.io sets `webviewTag:false` everywhere) [fact: electron.js webRequest block, 7 `webviewTag:false`/disable hits].
- Scoreboard ▲ = a host/kipc constraint that is not a per-app choice (`app.quit(): Promise<void>`, listener isolation, bounded sync deadlines, shadow getters) — exactly how KEL-72 chose [fact].
- Scoreboard ✘ = documented-never or tracked-unsupported, scored as a `fail` cell in the committed denominator; never hidden by a skip or retry (research 214 ratchet) [fact].

must_never: Emulate `remote`, arbitrary Chromium/V8 flags, `nodeIntegration:true` in a renderer, full CDP in production webviews, raw child_process/exec from strict roles, or app-selected updater feed URLs into a privileged updater (briefing never-list).

Ship a fake `sendSync` that is secretly async, or an unbounded one; it stays a blocking CALL with deadline, rate limit and dev warning (KEL-127, arch 02 §5).
Create a second process model: `utilityProcess.fork` is a request for a host-declared role; `MessageChannelMain` is a host-owned virtual port; PID is diagnostic only (arch 04 §3.1, 06 §1.2).
Let `keld migrate` silently select the `legacy` profile from Electron options (`sandbox:false`, package name); legacy requires an explicit Keld profile key with a printed forfeit (KEL-78).
Leak stack/endpoint/token material through `ipcMain.handle` error replies while matching Electron's message-only contract.
Run Electron's `spec/` tree as an oracle under Bun or copy its 3-retry CI policy (research 214).
Record a divergence silently: every ▲ needs a scoreboard row or quirks flag chosen in the PR with report wording (keld-compat AGENTS).
q1.confidence: high on layering, alias, destroyed-object and ordering rules (all grounded in specs or run probes); medium on sync-getter shadow policy (design choice, not yet specced); low on renderer sendSync mechanism (unknown until the WKWebView experiment runs).

q2.position:
Where the advantage actually comes from today is narrow and host-lane only; where compatibility costs is the two-hop, host-mediated, UI-thread-touching renderer IPC path plus facade round trips — and none of that is measured yet. Separate strictly:

MEASURED (immutable keld-benches cites, hello-class, not draw.io)
- Windows host RSS: Keld 19,552 KB vs Electron main 89,140 KB (−78%) — host/main process only; Electron won total process-tree RSS in the broader Windows measurement [fact].
- Windows paired MEM-IDLE: Keld host WS 22,788 KiB vs Tauri 26,856 KiB, median ratio 0.8484, CI95 [0.8469, 0.8495], publication-eligible — host lane only; host+Bun sum did NOT reproduce (Bun working set swings 2.22x while private bytes is 1.00x) -> INCONCLUSIVE under §5.1 [fact].
- Windows host exe 484,864 B vs Tauri 8,634,880 B [fact].
- First paint: Windows host-only `--hello` Keld 469 ms, Tauri 479, Electron 275 — Electron leads; floor is `CreateCoreWebView2Controller` (Chromium boot), Keld-attributable 3–6 ms; wry-bridge hypothesis refuted by A/B [fact]. macOS untraced double-rAF host-only proxy 342.911 ms vs ≤300 budget; not a score (host-only arm, raw JSON not in git) [fact].
- kipc small-message: Windows Bun<->Rust diagnostic p99 101.6 µs fresh / 100.5 µs warm — 1 session, 10k calls, 25-byte payload, `publication.eligible=false`; both marginally over the 100 µs budget and NOT a verdict; macOS/Linux unmeasured [fact].
- Bun extension-host bootstrap PoC (reference §28.3, private research): 53.3% sooner to Initialized, 42.8% lower RSS, 54.5% lower CPU — empty-extension workload only [fact as cited; not re-run here].

TARGET (arch 01 §5): installer ≤20 MB (bun) / ≤6 MB (none); cold start->first paint ≤300 ms; idle RSS 1 window ≤90 MiB (host+guardian+Bun, engine XPCs excluded); kipc p99 ≤100 µs; bulk ≥1 GB/s only with a shm lane; update patch ≤50 KB (no bytes-kind registry id yet); `keld dev` ≤2 s [fact].

PROJECTION (reference §30/§33): 75–87% smaller installer, 70–90% lower cold start, 40–70% lower total memory — arithmetic on targets vs a survey baseline; never a measurement [fact].

WHERE THE ADVANTAGE STRUCTURALLY COMES FROM [inference, consistent with §28/§31]: no bundled Chromium (disk, and the Windows host-RSS gap), a GC-free host that owns windows/brokers, a Bun role instead of Electron-as-Node for main-process JS, and binary framing with host mediation. Rust is not the advantage; the process topology is.

WHERE COMPATIBILITY COSTS PERFORMANCE (ranked by expected magnitude, all currently unmeasured)
1. Renderer IPC is two hops with two codecs and two UI-thread touches: page -> WKScriptMessageHandler (host main thread) -> kipc postcard SCV -> Bun -> kipc -> host main thread -> `evaluateJavaScript` into the content world. Electron is one Mojo hop. The live bridge admits ONE pending invoke per WebView and 4 KiB inline (KEL-142), so a facade must queue: draw.io's `rendererReq` is fire-and-forget with many in flight and its responses are `mainResp` pushes; Zettlr has 187 invoke sites and 49 `webContents.send` sites [fact]. Serialization latency = N x RTT, and every push is a main-thread `evaluateJavaScript` (draw.io's progress bar `_exec`s JS per tick) [fact].
2. Structured-clone codec: Electron serializes with SCA and throws on Functions/Promises/Symbols/WeakMaps/WeakSets/DOM objects [fact]. Keld's SCV sum type over postcard must encode Date/Map/Set/Error/TypedArray on both sides; large Buffers must hop to the `keld://c/` bulk lane with counted copies (arch 02 §3) — "binary codec" does not make a transfer zero-copy [fact]. Payloads >4 KiB (draw.io saves diagram XML through IPC) cannot ride the inline bridge at all today.
3. Facade round trips: every main-process call touching host state is a kipc CALL; sync getters are either shadow reads (free) or an Atomics.wait-blocked RTT (≥ the kipc p99, plus a worker wakeup). Chatty getter loops in app code become a visible cost.
4. Extra processes in the census: Keld adds guardian + Bun primary where Electron's main is one process; on Windows six WebView2 engine processes (329,138 KiB median) are excluded from both arms but a real app still pays Chromium [fact]. The product census (host+guardian+Bun) is unmeasured on macOS [fact].
5. Preload/compat user-script injection per navigation and CSP injection — small but on the paint path; must be attributed, not assumed.

The only honest sentence today is reference §34's: substantially smaller native-host memory, promising Bun efficiency, startup and total-process performance still being validated.

q4.kill_risk: The renderer<->main IPC lane. Keld's invariants fix the topology — webview and Bun role never connect directly; the host mediates every frame (arch 02 §1) — so every Electron `ipcRenderer.send/invoke` and every `webContents.send` is two hops with two codecs and two host main-thread touches (WKScriptMessageHandler receive, `evaluateJavaScript` push), where Electron is one Mojo hop. The live bridge admits one pending invoke per WebView, caps inline payload at 4 KiB, and has no push lane (KEL-142) [fact]. The corpus is chatty-concurrent and payload-heavy: draw.io's preload is fire-and-forget `rendererReq` with many in flight and `mainResp` pushes back, plus file contents through IPC and per-tick `executeJavaScript` progress; Zettlr has 187 invoke, 49 send and 6 sendSync sites [fact]. If the measured two-hop path is ms-class per message, serializes under the credit window, or saturates the host main thread under a save/open burst, then (a) draw.io is observably slower than on Electron, (b) the 'compat layer beats Electron's native IPC' design goal (arch 02) is falsified, and (c) the only fixes that restore Electron-class latency — a direct wv<->Bun link, or blocking the UI thread — violate the four uniques. That makes it the one risk that cannot be deferred, scoped around, or declared ▲ without the program's performance premise collapsing. Runner-up (claim-narrowing, not fatal): draw.io's ambient Node fs/child_process in main forces an explicit `legacy` profile, so the first migration proof cannot demonstrate the zero-ambient-authority unique. Explicitly NOT the killer for this corpus: WKWebView Service Workers on custom schemes (WebKit 206741 is still NEW, but draw.io desktop loads file:// where Chromium has no SW either, and neither draw.io nor Zettlr references `serviceWorker` [fact/inference]); native addons (draw.io has none); `<webview>` (disabled by draw.io); updater (disable via env).
q4.experiment: Cheapest discriminator, runnable on the shipped macOS bridge (#351) before any facade exists, ~2–3 days: (1) Register two metric ids in gyldlab/keld-benches `schema/metrics.v1.json` first (01 §5.1 forbids quoting unregistered metrics): `IPC-WV-RTT` (renderer-observed round trip, renderer monotonic clock) and `HOST-MAIN-OCCUPANCY` (os_signpost interval per routed message). (2) Arm K: a hello page over `window.keld.invoke` to a Bun `@keld/api` echo handler; add a scratch push path (host `evaluateJavaScript` in the content world) — a diagnostic branch, not product code. Workloads: W1 1,000 sequential 64 B invokes; W2 200 concurrent 1 KiB sends + 200 pushes back (draw.io `rendererReq`/`mainResp` shape) under the one-pending floor and under a 16/64 credit window; W3 one 2 MiB payload via `keld://c/` streaming with copies counted; W4 100 push messages per second for 10 s (progress-bar shape). (3) Arm E: electron-quick-start on Electron 44.4.5, same Mac, same session, same four workloads over `ipcRenderer.invoke/send` + `webContents.send`. (4) Statistic: p50/p99 with session-block bootstrap CI, fresh-process and warm-cache separate, ≥20 sessions; main-thread occupancy per message; copies per transfer for W3. Kill criterion (pre-registered): Keld W2 p99 > 5x Electron's, or W4 main-thread occupancy > 20% of a 16.7 ms frame, or W3 needs > 2 copies renderer->Bun. Pass criterion: W1 p99 within 2x and W2 within 3x of Electron with a credit window ≥16, W3 ≤ 2 copies.
q4.fallback: Ordered, all inside the four uniques: (1) Replace one-pending with a bounded credit window (KEL-80 backpressure owner) and coalesce pushes into one `evaluateJavaScript` per run-loop turn carrying a batched frame — removes the N x RTT serialization and the per-message main-thread hop; re-measure. (2) Route payloads > 4 KiB over the `keld://c/{channel}` streaming lane with counted copies (arch 02 §3), and make the SCV codec forward Bun->renderer frames without re-encoding at the host (host validates header/length/guard, does not decode the body) — a wire-protocol gate spec. (3) If still failing, do not add a direct wv<->Bun link and do not block the UI thread. Narrow the claim honestly instead: the compat profile documents an IPC latency class as ▲, the scoreboard records `primary_workflow` cells that time out as fails, and the corpus denominator targets apps whose IPC is request/response-shaped; chatty-push apps (progress bars, watchers) are advised to use the typed `@keld/api` stream channel in `keld migrate` diagnostics. (4) If even (3) cannot make draw.io's save/open acceptable, the program's performance premise is falsified for this corpus and the honest output is an approved spec for a host-side authenticated fast path (host still mints identity and evaluates the guard per frame, but forwards app-link bytes to the engine lane without copying into Bun-side codec) — a new wire-protocol and architecture review, recorded as a new invariant rather than an exception.

q1.position: Clone Electron's observable contract as a THIN, TESTED FACADE over generic Keld primitives, with every layer placed by a single question — 'who must own the handle to make this observable?' — and never by API family. Concretely: (1) `@keld/electron` (TS) is a pure consumer of `@keld/api` (KEL-142 §4.3 already forbids a duplicate transport); it holds Electron-shaped classes, EventEmitter semantics, destroyed-proxy state, the sync-getter snapshot/mirror, and the renderer shim SOURCE that is bundled into the user-script. It never frames kipc and never decides policy. (2) `keld-compat` (Rust) owns only what JS cannot fake: translating `webPreferences` into a `WebviewSpec` (preload path → isolated-world user-script, `additionalArguments` → synthesized `process.argv`, `contextIsolation:false`/`nodeIntegration:true` → refusal), the ordered per-app-link event stream (ready → window events → ipc EVENTs → before-quit → will-quit → quit on ONE link so cross-channel order matches Electron's single-threaded main), the cancellable-close state machine (host returns NO from `windowShouldClose:` immediately, forwards a cancellable `close` to Bun, closes only when Bun does not preventDefault — reproducing 'close before beforeunload/unload, closed after' without blocking the UI loop), file:// app-origin scoping via `loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL:` bound to the app code dir (this is draw.io's own `onBeforeRequest` file guard, compiled into host policy), static compilation of `session.webRequest` rules, `nativeImage` codecs, and host-minted `event.sender`/`senderFrame` identities. No Electron-ism may enter keld-core/keld-ipc (keld-compat AGENTS.md). (3) The renderer compat user-script is injected at document start in the isolated `WKContentWorld` that KEL-142 already installs (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs uses `WKUserScript…inContentWorld`, `defaultClientWorld`, page-world fallback forbidden). It provides `require('electron')` → {ipcRenderer.send/on/once/invoke/postMessage, contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld, webFrame subset, webUtils.getPathForFile} and a `process` object {type:'renderer', contextIsolated:true, argv incl. additionalArguments, versions}. Nothing else is `require`-able: preload Node access (Zettlr's two `sandbox:false` windows) is ✘ documented-never. SYNC GETTERS, HONESTLY, three classes: (a) boot-static values (`app.getPath`, `getVersion`, `getName`, `getLocale`-after-ready, `isPackaged`, `process.versions`) come from a host-minted boot descriptor carried with HELLO/Ready and are plain local reads — this is mandatory, because draw.io constructs `electron-store` at module top level (electron.js:30) and electron-store's constructor calls `app.getPath('userData')` synchronously before `ready`; (b) mirrored state (`win.getBounds/isMaximized/isFocused`, `screen.getAllDisplays/getPrimaryDisplay` — draw.io window-bounds.js:740, `nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors`) is a facade shadow fed by host EVENTs with optimistic local apply on setters; 'set then get' matches Electron, 'OS mutated then get' can be one event stale → scoreboard ▲ with a sequence test; (c) genuinely blocking calls with side effects (`dialog.showMessageBoxSync` — draw.io electron.js:876, `clipboard.readText` — :4286, renderer `sendSync`) are a BLOCKING CALL WITH DEADLINE exactly as KEL-127/architecture 02 §5 rule: the Bun main thread parks on `Atomics.wait` over a SharedArrayBuffer while a dedicated kipc thread performs CALL/REPLY; deadline expiry throws a `KELD-IPC-006`-mapped error instead of hanging; rate-limited and dev-warned. Bun 1.4.2 main-thread `Atomics.wait` works (probe returned `timed-out`, no throw). Renderer `sendSync` has NO native synchronous primitive in WKWebView (script-message handlers are async); the only candidate is a synchronous XHR against the host scheme handler [inference] — until an experiment proves it, renderer `sendSync` is ✘ with a migrate fix-it to `invoke`, not a silently-async ▲ (KEL-127 explicitly says an async replacement changes the caller contract). DESTROYED OBJECTS: facade objects are proxies over host handle ids; the host emits an ordered `Destroyed` EVENT; the proxy flips to destroyed and every subsequent member access throws synchronously `Object has been destroyed` BEFORE any kipc, `isDestroyed()` is a local read, `webContents.send` to a navigated/destroyed generation is dropped with a dev warning (Electron: `senderFrame` 'May be null if accessed after the frame has either navigated or been destroyed'). EVENT ORDERING is a contract tested as SEQUENCES with negative controls (keld-compat AGENTS), citing the pinned doc: `close` → DOM beforeunload/unload → `closed`; `destroy()` skips `close`; `app.quit()` → `before-quit` → per-window close → `will-quit` → `quit`; `quitAndInstall()` emits `before-quit` AFTER windows close. SURFACING DIVERGENCE, one rule: a `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag only when two legitimate behaviors exist and the app must choose (both arms tested — e.g. `appOrigin: 'file' | 'keld-resource'`, `webRequest: 'static-compiled'`, `reportElectronVersion`); scoreboard ▲ when Keld differs for everyone by design, with a conformance cell whose `expected_verdict` is 'fail' and an `intentional_divergence` note (the KEL-237 corpus already has this shape for `app.quit` → Promise<void>); ✘ when unsupported, split into documented-never (security) and tracked (ticket), always with a migrate fix-it. Never silent: under `keld dev` the recorder prints each ▲/✘ the app actually hit. MUST NEVER BE EMULATED (I would refuse a PR that does): `remote`; `nodeIntegration:true` or `sandbox:false` Node access in any renderer/preload; session permission default-allow (a missing handler is a deny with a KELD-GUARD diagnostic); `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` as app-minted privilege bits (scheme privileges are declared in host config and reviewed); unfiltered `shell.openExternal` (goes through the `shell.open` allowlist); app-selected `autoUpdater.setFeedURL` into a privileged updater (facade accepts the call only if it names the built-in feed identity, otherwise throws); raw `child_process` from strict roles (`shell.spawn` reviewed grants only — draw.io's `attrib.exe` spawn and `execFile` sites); ASAR/Chromium-internal filesystem layouts (draw.io inspects `userData/Local Storage/leveldb`, electron.js:58 — it already treats absence as fresh install, so ▲ not ✘); V8/Chromium flags; full CDP in production webviews; `<webview>` on macOS v1 (draw.io itself sets `webviewTag:false` on all five windows and `preventDefault`s `will-attach-webview`). Also refuse: spoofing `process.versions.electron` to a real Electron version by default — only an explicit `reportElectronVersion` quirk tied to the declared 44.x baseline, because ecosystem libraries gate on it [unknown which ones in this corpus].

q2.position: Keld's advantage, as far as evidence goes TODAY, is narrow and process-shaped, not language-shaped: (measured, narrow) a far lighter native main process on Windows (19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB), a smaller host binary lane, and a faster/lighter Bun bootstrap in one empty-extension-host PoC (53% sooner Initialized, 43% lower RSS). Everything else — installer ≤20 MB, cold start ≤300 ms, idle RSS ≤90 MiB, kipc p99 ≤100 µs, ≤50 KB patches — is TARGET or PROJECTION, and on the one first-paint comparison we have Electron WINS (275 ms vs Keld 469 ms host-only diagnostic on WebView2). Compatibility is not free and the cost lands in exactly the places Electron does in-process: (1) every main-process Electron API call that Electron services as a synchronous C++ binding becomes a Bun→host kipc CALL (~47 µs p50 / ~101 µs p99 Windows diagnostic) — BrowserWindow constructors, setBounds, Menu.setApplicationMenu, dialog, clipboard; draw.io's main is 4,543 lines of such calls; (2) sync emulation adds a thread hop and park/wake on top of the round trip and freezes the Bun event loop for its duration (same as Electron freezes, but Keld pays the cross-process latency too); (3) the structured-clone-compatible SCV codec runs in JS on the Bun side and in Rust on the host, twice per webContents.send/invoke, versus Electron's single native V8 serializer — allocation on a path architecture 02 §6 says must be allocation-free in steady state; (4) chatty `webContents.send` is Bun→host→webview, two hops and one SCV decode in the renderer user-script (draw.io 15 call sites, Zettlr 49); (5) app-installed `session.webRequest` hooks (draw.io installs BOTH onHeadersReceived and onBeforeRequest) would make every resource load a host→Bun round trip on the first-paint critical path unless compiled statically — a quirk, not free fidelity; (6) the preload user-script and `require('electron')` shim add document-start work on every navigation. WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST, in this order and under architecture 01 §5.1 census rules: (A) the macOS PRODUCT census hello (keld-host + guardian + Bun primary; WebKit XPCs excluded and reported separately; clock armed before host spawn to PAINT-OPPORTUNITY; 30 fresh-process samples with bootstrap CI; RSS in binary units with private footprint as the reproducibility control) — it is UNMEASURED and nothing about macOS may be claimed until it exists; (B) the COMPAT TAX as a paired diagnostic lane, not a budget row: electron-quick-start through `@keld/electron` vs the identical page through `@keld/api` hello, same binary/machine/cache class — Δpaint and ΔRSS are the facade cost; (C) kipc small-message p99 on macOS per §5.1 (product Bun client, handshake excluded, ≥20 sessions × 100k calls, 6-byte and 1,024-byte tiers, upper CI bound vs 100 µs) plus an IPC-COMPAT lane: SCV encode+decode cost per tier against raw postcard echo, and a sendSync lane (Atomics.wait park→REPLY→wake) reported as round trip with its own distribution; (D) webContents.send fan-out: messages/s and round trip (renderer echoes back via invoke) at 6 B / 1 KiB / 64 KiB, because one-way cross-process timing has no shared clock; (E) draw.io end-to-end on the same Mac: Electron 44.4.5 vs Keld, time to first interactive editor, idle RSS by role, and resource-load count — the only number a migrating maintainer actually cares about; (F) update bytes for a 1-line draw.io JS change (deterministic: 1 sample + 1 rebuild) against electron-builder's blockmap differential, not against a full installer. Each decomposition must separate census (which processes), work (what the app did), queue/copy (hops, serializations, copies), clock (who timed, which domain), statistic (median/p99 + CI) and artifact (raw JSON in keld-benches).

q4.kill_risk: The updater handoff. If an installed Electron app's own electron-updater/Squirrel.Mac cannot be made to install and relaunch a Keld-built bundle from the app's EXISTING feed (and the Windows NSIS/Squirrel equivalent), then every migrated app strands its installed base at the last Electron release, and no maintainer of a shipping app will flip the switch no matter how good the API scoreboard is — the program fails on adoption, not on compatibility. Architecture 04 §7 already calls this 'the trap every migrator hits' and promises a 'bridge release recipe', but nothing in the repo tests it: keld-update owns only Keld→Keld full-package activation (KEL-53), and the feed formats are disjoint (electron-builder: latest-mac.yml + zip, sha512, Squirrel.Mac JSON; Keld: updates.json + ed25519 .sig + full.zst). draw.io specifically runs autoUpdater with autoDownload=false, user-prompted downloadUpdate(), quitAndInstall() on a timer, and `publish: github`, so its users are on exactly this path. Runner-up kill risks, in order: (2) renderer synchronous IPC on WKWebView (Zettlr's pinia config store and electron-store's renderer path block on sendSync at startup; WKWebView has no synchronous native call — if neither sync-XHR-to-scheme-handler nor DOM-event cross-world calls work, 'config-only' is false for the second corpus app); (3) persistent profile identity (KEL-135) — if WKWebsiteDataStore identity or localStorage persistence is not stable across launches, draw.io users lose all settings on first Keld launch; (4) WKWebView Service Workers on custom schemes (WebKit 206741) — unknown whether draw.io's desktop build registers a SW (ElectronApp.js lives in the un-cloned submodule); (5) event-ordering fidelity of close/beforeunload/closed across an async host boundary; (6) native addons (none in draw.io; Zettlr's fsevents/nodehun are version-qualified evidence problems, not program killers). The webview tag is NOT a kill risk for this corpus: draw.io disables it and Zettlr does not use it.
q4.experiment: A two-day, zero-product-code spike on one Mac, in the scratchpad and keld-benches only: (1) build electron-quick-start with electron-builder (mac zip + dmg, `publish: generic` to a local HTTP directory), code-signed with a Developer ID, with electron-updater `autoDownload=true`, version 1.0.0; install and run it once so it checks the feed. (2) Produce the 'bridge' release 1.0.1: a Keld hello `.app` (the KEL-141 prebuilt host + pinned Bun; today the staged keld-host is acceptable as a stand-in) signed with the SAME Team ID and SAME CFBundleIdentifier/CFBundleName, zipped, with a hand-written `latest-mac.yml` carrying its sha512/size — i.e. a non-Electron bundle served through the Electron app's own feed. (3) Observe, with receipts: does electron-updater download it (sha512 ok), does Squirrel.Mac/ShipIt accept and swap the bundle (Console.app ShipIt log, codesign -dv of the result), does the relaunched process be the Keld host, and does the Keld host then successfully read its own `updates.json` on next check. Negative controls: (a) same bundle signed with a different Team ID (expect refusal — proves the check exists), (b) unsigned bundle (expect refusal), (c) bundle identifier mismatch (record outcome). (4) Repeat the cheapest Windows arm later: electron-updater NSIS path running a Keld-built NSIS installer through latest.yml (electron-updater verifies the Windows signature publisher name — record whether a differently-named signer is rejected). Discriminating output: a yes/no per OS on 'the final Electron release can hand off to Keld automatically', plus the exact validation that gates it. This also tells us whether `@keld/electron-updater` needs to emulate anything other than events (checking-for-update, update-available, download-progress, update-downloaded, error) on top of KEL-53 full-package activation.
q4.fallback: If Squirrel.Mac refuses a non-Electron bundle (or requires an Electron-shaped Contents layout), the bridge becomes a CHAINLOADER final Electron release, not a direct swap: the last Electron version of the app ships with a tiny Keld-authored module that (a) fetches Keld's signed `updates.json` + `.sig` for the configured channel/target, verifies the ed25519 signature and blake3 of `full.zst` exactly as keld-update does (reuse the Rust verifier compiled to a sidecar or re-implemented ONLY with a shared golden-vector test corpus — one source of truth for the vectors), (b) stages the Keld `.app` next to the current bundle, (c) shows one unavoidable 'draw.io is moving to a new runtime' dialog on `update-downloaded`, and (d) on `quitAndInstall` runs a host-owned installer step (macOS: a signed helper doing the atomic bundle swap into the same path; Windows: the Keld NSIS/MSI installer in silent mode) and relaunches. The feed server serves both formats for the whole transition window (arch 04 §7). If even that is unacceptable to an app (no code change allowed in the final Electron release), the honest answer is a documented one-time manual install with `keld migrate` printing the stranded-user warning — and I, as the maintainer, would not migrate that app yet. Fallbacks for the runner-ups: renderer sendSync → ✘ + migrate fix-it to `invoke` (Zettlr becomes 'small code change', scored honestly as not config-only); persistent profile → block the draw.io proof on KEL-135 rather than ship a first launch that loses settings; SW on custom schemes → `appOrigin:'file'` or an HTTPS loopback adapter with navigation-bound capability (arch 05 §2) instead of a custom scheme.

q1.position: Clone Electron's observable contract, not its object graph, and put each layer where its authority already lives. (1) `@keld/electron` (TS, Bun primary) is the ONLY place Electron's object model exists: `app`, `BrowserWindow`, `WebContents`, `ipcMain`, `Menu`, `dialog`, etc. are TS classes over `@keld/api` (KEL-142 freezes `app`, `channels.handle`, link). The facade owns per-object lifecycle state machines (`live → closing → destroyed`) driven by host EVENT frames (`WindowClosing(w)`/`WindowClosed(w)` already named in KEL-75 T4a), emits Electron events in Electron order, and after `closed`/`destroyed` throws `Object has been destroyed` on property reads and returns `isDestroyed()==true` exactly as the pinned docs say. Ids (`webContents.id`, window ids) are host-minted principal/generation ids surfaced as integers; the facade never mints them. `require('electron')` must resolve for node_modules too (draw.io's electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu/electron-updater all require it): the alias-probe proves tsconfig `paths` remaps a node_modules CJS `require('electron')` under Bun 1.4.2 [fact], so `keld migrate` writes `tsconfig.json paths` as the runtime resolver and `bunfig.toml` only as the named file (arch 04 §3 v0 note). (2) `keld-compat` (Rust) holds host-side SEMANTIC ADAPTERS only: translating Electron shapes (`protocol.handle` → `WebEngine::register_scheme`; `setWindowOpenHandler`/`will-navigate` → keld-wv navigation policy callbacks; `printToPDF` → `WKWebView.createPDF` (macOS 11+); `session` subset → keld-wv verified profile; dialogs/menu/clipboard/shell → keld-native brokers) and the close/closed/beforeunload sequencing. It consumes keld-core's window registry (TARGET, not live) and asks keld-guard; it owns no policy, no registry, no second IPC. (3) The renderer compat user-script runs in the isolated `WKContentWorld` seam KEL-142 already requires: it hosts the app's preload as CJS with a `require('electron')` + `process.{argv,platform,versions,type='renderer'}` shim (draw.io's preload reads `process.argv` for `additionalArguments` and uses `window.localStorage`/`window.navigation`), implements `ipcRenderer.send/on/once/removeListener/invoke` over `window.keld.send/on/invoke`, and implements `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` as a page-world relay: values copied+frozen, functions proxied by request id, Promises forwarded (pinned contextBridge doc). The relay accepts no broader shape than `window.keld.invoke` (KEL-142 §5.1). Wire codec: ONE structured-clone-value (SCV) sum type generated by the existing KEL-98 echo-codegen owner (arch 02 §5), covering Electron's Structured Clone domain (Date, Map/Set, TypedArray/Buffer, Error) and throwing on Functions/Symbols/Promises/DOM objects exactly as Electron does; no second IDL. SYNC, honestly: (a) main-process sync getters are two mechanisms, chosen per API on the scoreboard: a host-pushed state mirror for host-authoritative state the host already publishes (focused window, bounds, fullscreen/maximized, displays, `nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors`, `isDestroyed`) — reads are local and consistent to the last EVENT, staleness is a documented ▲ — and a true blocking CALL for value fetches that cannot be mirrored (`clipboard.readText`, `dialog.showMessageBoxSync`) implemented as a worker-thread kipc link + `Atomics.wait` with a deadline, rate-limited and dev-warned (sync-probe: Bun 1.4.2 main thread `Atomics.wait` returns `ok` after a 50 ms worker notify in 59.87 ms [fact]). (b) renderer `ipcRenderer.sendSync` stays a blocking call with a deadline per KEL-127 (never silently async); the only browser-legal blocking primitive on WKWebView is a synchronous XHR to the host scheme handler (`Atomics.wait` is forbidden on the main thread) — this is [inference] until the Q4 experiment proves it; if it fails, `sendSync` is ✘ with a fix-it, not an async impostor. draw.io has zero `sendSync` sites; Zettlr has 6 (`config-provider`/`citeproc-provider`), so this lands with the second candidate. EVENT ORDERING is tested as sequences, not outcomes (keld-compat AGENTS.md): `close` → engine `beforeunload`/`unload` → `closed`; `destroy()` skips `close` and guarantees `closed`; `before-quit` → windows close → `will-quit` → `quit`, with `window-all-closed` skipped on explicit `app.quit()`; `ready` only after the first event-loop tick; `open-file`/`second-instance` exactly-once typed delivery (research 186 gap 2). Per-channel FIFO is a kipc property; cross-channel ordering between EVENT and REPLY is pinned by conformance vectors against Electron 44.4.5 fixtures, and stage-only-passers ratchet per note 214. ERRORS: `ipcMain.handle` throw → renderer rejection whose Error carries only `message` (pinned ipc-main doc) — Keld maps kipc `ERR CallError{code,message}` to that exact string shape, keeping `code` on a Keld-namespaced property; guard denials (`KELD-GUARD002`) surface as rejections with fix guidance, never as `allow`. DIVERGENCE SURFACING, one rule: quirks flag in `keld.compat.ts` when both behaviors are legitimate and the APP must choose (`windowOpenHandler` strictness, `sendSync` policy, `fileUrlRoot` → host-scheme mapping, `menuAccelerators`); scoreboard ▲ when the divergence is a host/kipc constraint identical for every app (`app.quit(): Promise<void>`, per-listener try/catch, getter-mirror staleness, `sendSync` rate limit); ✘ when documented-never or tracked (`webRequest` on remote http(s) — WKWebView exposes no subresource interception, `sandbox:false`, `nodeIntegration:true`). Every ▲/✘ is a row in the compat scoreboard tied to a `keld.compat.evidence/v1` cell; a migrate report prints them; nothing is silent (KEL-127).

q2.position: KELD's advantage is structural and already partly measured in two narrow places: the native host process is small (Windows direct-COM session: Keld main 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB [fact, main process only]; macOS WK hosts cluster at ~95–100 MiB main vs Electron 43.4.0 main 134.8 MiB plus 200 MB of Chromium helpers [fact, different engine]) and Bun boots Node-shaped work faster than Electron-as-Node in the VS Code extension-host PoC (53.3% sooner to Initialized, 42.8% lower child RSS [fact, narrow]). Package size follows from not shipping Chromium (Electron hello zip 122 MB vs Tauri .app 8.3 MB on the same table [fact]). Nothing else is measured: cold start is currently LOST on Windows (Electron 275 ms vs Keld 469 ms, host-only `--hello`, controller-creation floor is Chromium's) and unmeasured as a product-census number on macOS (342.9 ms untraced `--hello` proxy, raw JSON gap); total-tree RSS was won by Electron on Windows; kipc p99 is a single-session Windows diagnostic (101.6/100.5 µs, publication.eligible=false); macOS/Linux kipc are unmeasured. COMPATIBILITY COSTS PERFORMANCE in five attributable places, and I will not let any of them be hand-waved: (1) Facade round trips — every Electron sync getter that becomes a blocking CALL costs ≥1 kipc RTT (~46–48 µs p50 measured on Windows) plus a Bun main-thread stall; the mirror strategy removes the RTT for host-published state but adds EVENT traffic for every focus/bounds/theme change. (2) Renderer path is two hops (page world → isolated world → WKScriptMessage/XPC → host → UDS → Bun) versus Electron's one Mojo hop, and KEL-142's envelope encodes payload bytes as a JSON array of 0..255 with a 4096-byte cap: ~3–4× byte inflation and a hard functional ceiling that draw.io's diagram-XML IPC (`rendererReq`/`mainResp`) will exceed. `ipcRenderer.invoke` RTT may be SLOWER than Electron; that is a measurement, not a defect of the thesis, but it must be on the table. (3) Structured-clone codec — a postcard SCV encoder written in JS (Bun and page) may lose to the engine's native JSON; arch 02 names a JSON fallback codec; the choice is per-measurement, not per-ideology. (4) Chatty `webContents.send` (Zettlr: 49 sites; draw.io: 15) is one host EVENT plus one `evaluateJavaScript`/content-world post per message; per-message engine injection cost on WKWebView is [unknown]. (5) Cold start grows by the facade's module graph (Bun loading `@keld/electron` + draw.io's 5.5k-line main + electron-store/-log) before the first window request, and the product census (01 §5.1) starts the clock at process spawn, so facade load time IS first-paint time. Measurement discipline: apply the 01 §5.1 census rows verbatim — product boot (host + guardian + Bun primary + facade), never `--hello`; one monotonic clock armed before spawn to the `PAINT-OPPORTUNITY` beacon; `fresh-process` and `warm-cache` as separate classes; 30 valid samples with bootstrap CI; RSS = keld-owned processes only with WebKit XPCs reported as a mandatory companion diagnostic (for a fair vs-Electron comparison also publish the total tree, labeled as such); kipc client-timed with handshake excluded, ≥20 sessions × 100k calls for a score. Separate census / work / queue-copy / clock / statistic / artifact per the atomic protocol. Claim ladder stays A measured / B target / C projection (reference §32), never blended.

Consume the spine's task-level artifacts (#322/#323/#325): KEL-142's content-world bridge and `@keld/api` surface are the renderer seam; KEL-141's prebuilt CLI/host is the launch vehicle; KEL-140 and KEL-143 are NOT prerequisites for the first migration proof because draw.io's main process does its own Node `fs` work and the proof runs under the visibly labeled legacy profile (KEL-75 AC6 / KEL-127: unsupported strict combos get an explicit diagnostic + labeled legacy profile; dev-permissive + recorder is the 03 §3 destination and does not exist yet). q4.kill_risk: The system-engine origin/resource model on WKWebView, not any facade gap. Electron apps assume Chromium's `file://` semantics (draw.io loads `file://${codeDir}/index.html?...` and relies on same-directory subresources, almost certainly XHR to `resources/dia*.txt` and other local files [inference: drawio webapp submodule absent from the clone], a `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` file allowlist and header-injected CSP). WKWebView's public API offers `loadFileURL(_:allowingReadAccessTo:)` (a read grant, not a Chromium origin model), no subresource interception, and the only alternative — serving app content through a custom scheme via `register_scheme`/WKURLSchemeHandler — changes the origin (localStorage keys like draw.io's `.configuration` are per origin), must reproduce `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` semantics by hand, and has no Service Worker support (WebKit bug 206741, status NEW since 2020). If median Electron apps cannot run their local content through either path on WKWebView, Keld is forced to the planned CEF pinned engine, which collapses the installer/RSS thesis (Electron 122 MB zip vs 8 MB WK app) — i.e. the program keeps compatibility OR performance, not both. Everything else named (sendSync, native addons, event ordering, Bun compat, webview tag, updater) is bounded engineering Keld owns; this one is owned by Apple.
q4.experiment: Two-day harness in the scratchpad (no Keld repo writes): check out the drawio webapp submodule at the pinned desktop commit 2edf9fb and drive a bare WKWebView (reuse keld-wv's wkwebview hello or a 150-line objc2/Swift shell) on macOS 26.5 through three arms, capturing console/errors via WKUserContentController: Arm A `loadFileURL(index.html?...)` with `allowingReadAccessTo: webapp dir`; Arm B the same tree served by a `keld://` WKURLSchemeHandler returning CORS + draw.io's exact CSP header; Arm C Arm B plus a registered Service Worker if the webapp registers one (observe `navigator.serviceWorker.register` outcome). Observables (each falsifiable): (1) editor reaches its load-finished signal (the preload's `app-load-finished` send — stub `ipcRenderer` to log it); (2) XHR/fetch to `resources/dia.txt` and plugin/stencil files succeed; (3) `localStorage` persists across relaunch under the same origin; (4) `window.navigation` presence (preload guards it, so absence is tolerable); (5) sync XHR to the scheme handler returns within a deadline (this also decides the Q1 renderer `sendSync` mechanism); (6) `createPDF` of export3.html renders a diagram (byte-compare to Electron `printToPDF` on the same machine as a fidelity diagnostic). Run the same six observables in Electron 44.4.5 as the oracle. Decision rule: Arm A or B passes (1)(2)(3) → risk retired for draw.io, record the chosen arm as the `fileUrlRoot` quirks default; only B passes → `file://` loads are ▲ remapped to the host scheme by migrate (config-only, origin-change documented); none pass → kill condition met for system-engine-first on this app.
q4.fallback: If Arm B passes but A fails: host-scheme serving becomes the default resource path (already the arch 05 §2 destination: host-mediated resource adapter with navigation-bound capability), `file://` is a ▲ remap in `keld.compat.ts`, Service-Worker-dependent apps are ✘ on macOS system engine and routed to KEL-79's HTTPS/loopback adapter evaluation. If both fail for draw.io: do not patch around it — invoke the engine-policy insurance already in arch 05 §1 (`engine: { mac: 'pinned' }` CEF opt-in per app, build-time fetched, app owns its security updates), publish draw.io's cells under a separate `engine: pinned` lane so the scoreboard never blends system-engine and pinned-engine results, re-run the Q2 baselines under CEF and let the measured numbers decide whether the performance claim survives for that profile. If the webapp needs Chromium-only features beyond resource loading, draw.io is reclassified per #313 (Zettlr first, draw.io deferred) with the evidence attached — a candidate swap, not a thesis change. What I refuse as fallback: a `file://` 'universal access' private WebKit preference (SPI, not public API), disabling CSP injection, or letting the page talk to Bun directly.

q1.position: Clone Electron's OBSERVABLE contract as three single-owner layers and refuse to clone its authority model. (1) `@keld/electron` is a pure-TS facade that consumes `@keld/api` (KEL-142 §4.3: the lifecycle transport must not be duplicated in both packages); every Electron class (app, BrowserWindow, WebContents, Menu, Tray, dialog…) is a TS state machine mirroring host-owned state, fed by one ordered kipc EVENT stream per link (arch 02 §5 'ordering per channel'). (2) `keld-compat` (Rust) owns only what JS cannot fake and the host must arbitrate: close-request arbitration (`close` preventDefault needs the host to hold the window until Bun replies or a deadline fires), window parenting/modals, host-minted `sender`/`senderFrame` identity bound to the webview handle + last-committed navigation, response-header/CSP injection for host-served app bundles (draw.io's `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` CSP and `file://` allow-list have no WKWebView equivalent), `protocol` scheme registration into the engine, `nativeImage` codecs. (3) The renderer compat user-script (`ipcRenderer`, `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld`, `webFrame` subset) is injected as a `WKUserScript` at `AtDocumentStart` into the isolated `WKContentWorld` that `crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs` already uses (page-world fallback forbidden there), which gives Electron's 'preload runs before page scripts, isolated from the page' semantics for free; `contextBridge` maps to real isolated-world exposure on macOS, and the Electron type table (string/number/boolean/Object/Array/Error/Promise/Function; Symbol ✘; prototypes dropped) is the conformance oracle. Synchronous surfaces are handled honestly, not faked: main-process sync getters (`BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow`, `getAllWindows`, `isDestroyed`, `getBounds`, `nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors`, `app.getPath/getLocale/getVersion`) are served from a host-pushed replica that is updated by ordered EVENTs before the Electron-visible event fires (e.g. the replica marks Destroyed before `closed` is emitted), so no sync getter ever blocks on a CALL; if a getter cannot be replica-served it is a scoreboard ▲ returning stale-but-ordered state, never a hidden blocking call. `ipcRenderer.sendSync` is the one surface that cannot be reproduced over the WKScriptMessage bridge (async only); KEL-127 forbids turning it into a Promise, so the only honest states are: ✘ with a `keld migrate` fix-it (draw.io has zero `sendSync` sites, so the first proof needs none), or — only after the experiment proves it — a blocking CALL with deadline over a synchronous engine channel (sync XHR to a host scheme handler is a [lead], unverified), rate-limited and dev-warned per arch 02 §5. Destroyed-object semantics: a TS `Destroyed` state that makes every property/method throw `Object has been destroyed` (Electron base-window.md), `win.destroy()` skips `close`/`beforeunload`/`unload` but guarantees `closed`, `win.close()` emits `close` before DOM `beforeunload` and may be cancelled; the facade orders these from host events on one dispatch queue and the pinned-oracle fixtures assert the order. App lifecycle order (`before-quit` → window closes → `window-all-closed` → `will-quit` → `quit`; `ready` gating; macOS `activate`) is already the KEL-72/KEL-237 pattern and draw.io depends on `before-quit` running before `window-all-closed` (its `cmdQPressed` flag). Errors: `invoke` rejects with message-only Errors (Electron ipc-main.md), which is exactly what a kipc `ERR` frame → `Error(message)` yields; sender identity is host-minted, never caller-supplied (draw.io's `validateSender(e.senderFrame)` checks `frame.url.startsWith(codeUrl)`, so `senderFrame.url` must be the host's last-committed URL and `null` after navigation/destroy). Divergence surfacing has three disjoint owners: a `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag only when the app can legitimately choose between two guard-checked behaviors (windowOpenHandler strictness, sendSync policy, menu accelerator edge cases); scoreboard ▲ when the divergence is a host/kipc constraint no app can toggle (`app.quit(): Promise<void>`, per-listener try/catch isolation, `disableHardwareAcceleration` as a no-op); ✘ for documented-never or tracked gaps with a fix-it and issue. A flag can select behavior but can never widen authority; a ▲ can never be silent; a ✘ can never degrade to a stub that returns success.

q2.position: Keld's advantage is architectural, not linguistic (reference §28/§31): no bundled Chromium (installer), a lean host without a GC runtime (main-process RSS), Bun instead of Electron-as-Node for the JS coordinator (the narrow VS Code extension-host PoC), and a binary, host-mediated kipc control plane. What is MEASURED today is narrow: Windows direct-COM session main/native RSS KELD 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (host only, not total memory); Windows first paint KELD 469 ms vs Tauri 479 vs Electron 275 (Electron leads; the floor is Chromium boot inside CreateCoreWebView2Controller); macOS untraced double-rAF proxy 342.911 ms (not a ≤300 ms label); Windows Bun↔Rust kipc p99 101.6 µs fresh / 100.5 µs warm as a diagnostic that is NOT publication-eligible (1 session vs 20, 10k vs 100k calls, 41-byte frame not the 22-byte small tier); Bun canary 80.9 ms vs Electron-as-Node 177.7 ms to Initialized on an empty-extension bootstrap. TARGETS (arch 01 §5): ≤20 MB installer with Bun, ≤300 ms first paint, ≤90 MiB idle RSS (host+guardian+Bun, WebKit XPCs excluded), kipc p99 ≤100 µs, ≤50 KB patch, ≤2 s keld dev. PROJECTIONS (reference §30/§33, label as such): 75–87% smaller package, 40–70% lower total memory, ~order-of-magnitude IPC latency on that one path. Compatibility COSTS performance in five specific places, each a separate census atom: (a) Facade hop count: an Electron renderer→main call is one Mojo hop; in Keld `ipcRenderer.invoke` is wv-link JSON envelope (renderer→host, main-thread hop on WKWebView) + kipc postcard CALL (host→Bun) + the reverse, i.e. two hops and two codecs, and KEL-142's minimum slice admits ONE pending renderer invoke per WebView with a 4096-byte payload cap — Zettlr has 187 invoke sites and draw.io correlates `rendererReq`/`mainResp` with reqId, so the one-pending limit serializes real apps and must be replaced by a bounded pending map with credit (KEL-80) before any corpus number is meaningful. (b) Structured-clone codec: the wv-link envelope carries payload as a JSON array of 0..255 integers (≈3–4× byte inflation before postcard), then an SCV sum type; Buffer/TypedArray need the bulk lane, and research 16 falsified the 02 §3 'streaming, off-UI-thread, backpressured keld:// bulk plane' on macOS and Windows (chunked under credit on macOS, SharedBuffer on Windows, true stream only on WebKitGTK). (c) Chatty `webContents.send`: each is a host-routed EVENT delivered via `evaluateJavaScript_inFrame_inContentWorld` on the UI thread (macos_bridge.rs:802); Zettlr has 49 send sites; events/sec and UI-thread occupancy are unmeasured. (d) Sync emulation: replica-served getters cost one EVENT per state change (cheap but allocation on the Bun side); any blocking sendSync path blocks the renderer and must be rate-limited. (e) Node-compat in the strict profile: if Node `fs` sync calls in Electron main code are brokered over kipc, each becomes a round trip that Electron served in-process (draw.io uses fs.existsSync/readFile/writeFile/watchFile from main). Measure first, in this order, under arch 01 §5.1 census rules: 1) macOS kipc small-message p99 with the pinned echo vector (6-byte payload/22-byte frame) and representative 1,024-byte tier, product Bun client against the shipping app link, handshake excluded, ≥20 sessions × 100,000 calls, fresh-process and warm-cache separate, client-clock, block-bootstrap CI upper bound vs 100 µs — macOS and Linux are currently UNMEASURED. 2) A new 'facade RTT' lane (needs a metric-registry id in keld-benches before publication): `ipcRenderer.invoke→ipcMain.handle` end-to-end timed in the renderer's monotonic clock, same fixture run under Electron 44.4.5 as the differential arm; report hops and copies per call (census: renderer, host, Bun). 3) Idle RSS on the product census (host+guardian+Bun, WebKit XPCs excluded, private footprint companion lane; a >5% resident-sum swing between matched runs is INCONCLUSIVE — the Windows host+Bun diagnostic already failed to reproduce, 81.8 MiB vs 54.5 MiB). 4) Cold start → first paint on the product boot (host + guardian + Bun, window after authenticated HELLO), never the host-only --hello arm. 5) Installer compressed lane per keld-pack format (one sample + reproducibility rebuild) — Bun alone is 16.8 MB zstd-19, so the 20 MB budget is at risk before any app bytes. 6) Event fan-out: `webContents.send` events/sec at 10/100/1000 msg/s with UI-thread occupancy on WKWebView. Forbidden until measured: 'faster than Electron' in any form (Electron currently leads the only first-paint session), '≤100 µs IPC' as a pass (diagnostic, over budget, not eligible), any installer/update-size claim (unmeasured; no bytes-kind registry id), generalizing the Bun 53%/43%/55% PoC beyond its bootstrap workload, applying any component ratio to whole-app performance (reference §30.5 'Never apply that ratio to whole-app performance'), and any claim that compatibility is 'zero-cost' — the facade adds hops and codecs by construction.

q4.kill_risk: The strict-profile main process cannot run median Electron main code config-only. Electron's main is 'a Node.js environment… all of Node.js APIs' with ambient fs/net/child_process; Keld's unique #2 is a Bun role with ZERO ambient OS authority where every privileged operation is a typed host call. draw.io's main calls fs.existsSync/readFile/writeFile/stat/watchFile directly and its libraries (electron-store, electron-log) write files; Zettlr's main uses chokidar/fsevents, a native .node addon and `got`. Reproducing that transparently requires a `node:fs`/`node:child_process`/`node:net`-shaped facade over kipc brokers — including the SYNCHRONOUS Node fs API, which cannot be brokered without blocking the Bun thread on a CALL (Atomics.wait on a worker-fed SharedArrayBuffer is the only known primitive, unproven in Bun under Keld) — on top of Bun's own Node-compat layer, which already shows measured parent-side child_process divergences (KEL-77) and version-fragile N-API loading (KEL-215). The program dies on either horn: if strict is mandatory, 'config-only migration' is false for the median app; if the visibly-labeled legacy profile becomes the de facto runtime, Keld ships Electron's authority model on a different host and loses the security uniqueness that justifies the host/guard investment. Runner-ups that do not kill the program: WKWebView Service Workers on custom schemes (draw.io loads file://, no SW; pinned CEF is the documented escape), sendSync (0 draw.io sites), <webview> (Electron deprecates it), native addons (per-app, addon-worker path exists), updater bridge (late, KEL-53 owns).
q4.experiment: Cheapest discriminating experiment (one week, scratchpad only, no Keld changes): (1) Run draw.io's and Zettlr's main entry under plain Bun (pinned revision) with `electron` aliased to a recording stub that implements only app.whenReady and logs every Electron call, and with `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `node:net`, `node:os` wrapped by an interposition module that logs each call as sync/async, path/authority class, and whether it is on the startup path (before first window request). Output: an ambient-authority census per app (counts, sync share, startup share). (2) Re-run the same under KEL-78's macOS Seatbelt strict candidate profile (no fs outside the app bundle, no net, no spawn) and record the first failing call and whether the app survives to 'window requested'.
