q1.position: Clone Electron's observable contract as a three-layer facade with one owner per layer, and treat every API cell as a differential-oracle problem: (a) the oracle is a pinned Electron v44.4.5 doc sentence plus, where docs are silent, a committed golden transcript recorded from real Electron 44.4.5 running a Keld-owned fixture (immutable blob + sha256, per research 214 Table 3); (b) Keld runs the same fixture through `keld dev --headless` and diffs the ordered event transcript, not the outcome; (c) a cell is BEHAVIOR_MATCH only when the ordered transcript matches and the named negative control fails it. Layers: [1] `@keld/electron` (TS, Bun main role) owns every Electron object shape — EventEmitter semantics, the Live→Closing→Destroyed state machine behind `isDestroyed()`/`Object has been destroyed`, `event.sender`/`event.senderFrame` objects, the `el:*` channel namespace and the structured-clone-value (SCV) adapter — and is a pure consumer of generic `@keld/api` (KEL-142 §4.3 already moved lifecycle this way; no second transport owner). [2] `keld-compat` (Rust, in-host) owns only what JS cannot fake and must be sequenced by the owner of the native handle: close→beforeunload→closed ordering with a host→facade CALL (not EVENT) for the cancellable `close`, window parenting/modals, `will-attach-webview`, custom-scheme registry into the engine, `webContents` routing identity, nativeImage codecs, session subset. [3] Renderer compat user-script, injected by the host at document start in an isolated WKContentWorld on macOS (the mechanism KEL-142 already proves for `window.keld.invoke`), providing `require('electron')` → {ipcRenderer, contextBridge, webFrame subset}, `process.{type:'renderer', argv (additionalArguments), platform, sandboxed}` over `window.keld.invoke/send/on` (05 §2). Sync honesty: per-session-immutable getters (`app.getPath`, `getLocale`, `getVersion`, `isPackaged`, `screen` displays) are delivered in the Ready payload and are truly synchronous; mutable getters (`getBounds`, `isMaximized`, `isFullScreen`, `getFocusedWindow`, `nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors`) answer from a host-pushed mirror subscribed on first read, with an optimistic apply so `setBounds(b); getBounds()` returns `b`; this is a scoreboard ▲ ('mirror, consistent within one kipc round trip') with its own conformance test, never a fabricated value. `ipcRenderer.sendSync` must exist (02 §5, KEL-127) as a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited and dev-warned; on WKWebView there is no synchronous script-message return, so the only honest candidate is a synchronous XHR to a host WKURLSchemeHandler that forwards a kipc CALL and replies — renderer blocks (as in Electron), host does not; deadline expiry throws a typed error (▲: Electron has no deadline). Returning `undefined`/a Promise from `sendSync` is a silent downgrade and is refused. Errors: `ipcMain.handle` rejections reproduce Electron's observable (message-only Error) by default; typed `KELD-*` codes ride a dev-mode quirks flag, not the default. Divergence decision procedure: host/kipc/engine constraint that applies to every app → scoreboard ▲ with doc citation and a test asserting the divergence (pattern: `app.quit` Promise); behavior an app may legitimately want either way → `keld.compat.ts` quirks flag whose default is Electron's behavior unless security forbids it (e.g. `contextBridge.world`, `sendSync.rateLimit`, `windowOpenHandler.strict`, `webRequest.fileFilter→hostResourcePolicy`); documented-never → ✘ with a `keld migrate` fix-it. `keld migrate` prints ▲/✘ per call site and must print the KEL-74 claim shape, never a percentage: the `compat score: 91%` line in architecture 04 §1's sample report violates compat-scoreboard rule 4 and I refuse it. I also refuse import-success-as-pass: a module that loads is L0, not a cell pass.

Compatibility is where the facade spends that advantage back: (1) facade round trips — every Electron sync getter becomes a mirror subscription or a CALL, and `webContents.send` (9 sites draw.io, 49 Zettlr) becomes two hops (Bun→host EVENT, host→engine script message) instead of one Mojo hop, with every byte crossing the macOS main run loop; (2) the SCV codec — a renderer→main `invoke` is serialized three times (engine script-message JSON, host postcard SCV, Bun decode) versus Electron's single structured-clone; Buffer/TypedArray 'bulk lane refs' are copies because 02 §3's streaming claims were falsified (research 16); (3) sync emulation — a scheme-handler round trip on the main run loop plus rate-limit queueing; (4) preload user-script injection at document start on every app window adds to window-level first paint; (5) state mirroring for sync getters adds steady-state EVENT traffic unless subscribe-on-first-read. q4.kill_risk: The renderer-side bridge contract on non-Chromium engines: Electron promises a preload that runs before page scripts, in an isolated world, exposing a synchronous `contextBridge` whose functions are proxied with copied/frozen values, plus `ipcRenderer.sendSync` that blocks the renderer until the main reply. If WKWebView (macOS) and WebView2 (Windows) cannot deliver that observable contract, every app's renderer and preload code — not just its main process — needs code changes, and the program's promise ('config-only') fails for the median app, not for an edge case. Evidence of exposure: Windows has no isolated worlds at all (research 16: ⬛ CANNOT), macOS has no synchronous script-message return (the KEL-142 bridge is promise-based by construction), Zettlr calls `sendSync` at Pinia store initialization (startup-blocking), and draw.io's preload depends on `process.argv` additionalArguments and ordered `once`/`on` delivery. Runner-up risks I considered and rank lower for the first proof: WKWebView Service Workers on custom schemes (draw.io loads file://, Zettlr uses protocol.handle for images — doctor warning, not kill); strict-profile ambient fs in migrated mains (mitigated honestly by the labeled legacy profile); the updater bridge (distribution, deferrable); userland `require('electron')` resolution (disproved as a blocker by the alias probe); native addons (none in draw.io).
q4.experiment: A two-day spike on the live KEL-142 macOS bridge, no new crates: (a) inject draw.io's UNMODIFIED `src/main/electron-preload.js` as a WKUserScript at document start in an isolated WKContentWorld with `require('electron')` and `process` shims, serve draw.io's `index.html` from the app dir through the host resource adapter, and assert in a Bun `ipcMain.on('rendererReq')` fixture that `window.electron.request(...)` round-trips, that `mainResp` for request N arrives before any response to request N+1, and that `process.argv` contains `--initial-adaptive-colors=`; (b) the sync lane: from page JS issue `XMLHttpRequest` with async=false to a host-registered scheme (`keld-sync://call`) whose WKURLSchemeHandler forwards one kipc CALL to the Bun role and answers with the reply; record whether WebKit permits it from the main thread on a custom scheme, the RTT distribution over 1,000 calls, and that the host main run loop keeps ticking (host-side timer) while the renderer is blocked; (c) negative controls: a page script that overwrites `window.electron.request` must not alter isolated-world behavior; a reload mid-request must drop the stale `mainResp` (generation rotation); deadline expiry must throw a typed error, never hang. Discriminator: (a)+(b) pass → contextBridge ✔ and sendSync ▲ (deadline + rate limit) on macOS; (a) passes, (b) fails → sendSync is ✘ on macOS with a codemod fix-it and the config-only claim is scoped to apps with zero sendSync (draw.io qualifies); (a) fails on preload-first ordering or isolation → program-level redesign before any further facade work.
q4.fallback: Tiered and labeled, never silent: (1) macOS: isolated-world `contextBridge` async-only ✔; `sendSync` ✘ with `keld migrate` codemod (sendSync→await invoke) — draw.io stays config-only, Zettlr becomes an honest L1-style migration (6 call sites in 3 files) and its scoreboard row says so. (2) Windows WebView2: `contextBridge` emulated in the page world behind quirks flag `contextBridge.world='page'` (▲ 'bridge is tamperable by page code'); per 03/16 untrusted or remote content gets zero bridge. (3) If preload-before-page ordering cannot be guaranteed by user scripts, the host resource adapter serves the app's HTML with the preload bundle injected as the first script (▲ documented, same observable order). (4) Apps that need Chromium-exact bridge semantics choose the pinned-engine (CEF) option per 01 §6 and research 16 — opt-in, labeled, inheriting the Electron-style engine update duty, never the default. Each fallback is recorded as ▲/✘ with a conformance test asserting the divergence; none of them widens authority.

q1.position:
Clone the observable contract, not the machine. Five layers, each with exactly one owner, already named by architecture 04 §3 and KEL-142 §4.3 — this program adds no sixth layer. (1) `@keld/electron` (TS, Bun main role) is a thin facade over `@keld/api`: every Electron main-process class is a state-mirroring proxy whose mutations are kipc CALLs and whose events are host frames dispatched in arrival order on the one lifecycle reader. It owns Electron *shape*: EventEmitter API, `Object has been destroyed` throws, `isDestroyed()` as the only post-destroy method, `preventDefault()` cancellation on `close`/`before-quit`, Electron's default webPreferences (contextIsolation true, nodeIntegration false). (2) `@keld/api` owns generic lifecycle/channels/window handles; it never learns an Electron name. (3) `keld-compat` (Rust, host side) owns what JS cannot fake: window parenting/modal, `webContents` routing identity (host-minted sender principal → `event.sender`/`senderFrame`), `protocol`/`session` subsets mapped onto the arch 05 resource transport, nativeImage codecs, and the conformance suites (oracle = pinned Electron 44.4.5 docs + recorded Electron event sequences, never Electron's `spec/` tree — research 214 REFUSE). (4) Renderer compat user-script in `keld-wv`: the Electron preload runs in the isolated `WKContentWorld` (KEL-142 §5.1); `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` is emulated by serializing the exposed API *shape* and installing a page-world proxy that forwards function calls to the isolated world — the same functions-only, prototype-stripped, structured-clone-args contract Electron documents, so it is a ✔ with ▲ edge cases, not a fake. `ipcRenderer.send/on/once/invoke` ride `window.keld.invoke`/`send`/`on` (arch 05 §: `@keld/electron`'s renderer shim implements ipcRenderer/contextBridge over it). (5) `keld.compat.ts` quirks flags: per-app toggles only where both behaviors are defensible (windowOpenHandler strictness, sendSync policy, shim logging) — arch 04 §2/§3.5. 

Synchronous surfaces, honestly: (a) main-process getters that are constant after `ready` (`app.getPath`, `getVersion`, `getName`, `getLocale`, `screen.getPrimaryDisplay`) are delivered in the Ready snapshot and served from memory — exact, no round trip. (b) Mutable window getters (`getBounds/getSize/getPosition/isMaximized/isVisible/isFocused/getFocusedWindow/getAllWindows`) read a facade mirror that the host updates by ordered state events with a sequence number; the getter may lag the OS by in-flight events. That is a divergence Electron's in-process C++ getters do not have, so it is a scoreboard ▲ (not a quirks flag: callers cannot choose otherwise) with a conformance test asserting the mirror converges after the event that caused it. I refuse a blocking socket read inside Bun's event loop for getters — it would stall every other dispatch. (c) `dialog.showMessageBoxSync` etc. in main: a blocking CALL with deadline on the Bun side is acceptable (Bun main is not the UI thread) — ✔ with the deadline (`KELD-IPC-006`) as ▲. (d) Renderer `ipcRenderer.sendSync`: KEL-127 and arch 02 §5 rule it must stay a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned, no silent async downgrade. WKWebView's script-message channel is Promise-only, so a true block needs a synchronous XHR to a host-owned scheme handler [inference, unverified this session]; until that experiment passes, `sendSync` is ✘ on macOS with `keld migrate` naming each call site (Zettlr has 6; draw.io has 0). I refuse an async shim that returns a Promise from `sendSync` — it changes the caller contract silently. 

Destroyed-object semantics: the host emits `WindowDestroyed(gen)`; the facade flips a `destroyed` flag and every method except `isDestroyed()` throws `Object has been destroyed` (Electron 44.4.5 BrowserWindow doc). `win.destroy()` is a distinct host op from `win.close()` because Electron guarantees `closed` without `close`/`beforeunload` for destroy and the opposite for close; the host contract must expose both or the facade cannot be honest. Event ordering: one totally ordered per-window stream (`close` → beforeunload cancel path → `closed`; `ready` → `window-all-closed` → `before-quit` → `will-quit` → `quit`), tested as sequences per `crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md`, with the KEL-72 per-listener try/catch isolation kept as a recorded ▲. 

Divergence surfacing rule (already practiced on the scoreboard): ✔ when the documented Electron behavior is reproduced and a conformance fixture cites the doc; ▲ scoreboard when the divergence is a host/kipc fact no app can toggle (Promise `app.quit`, listener isolation, getter mirror lag, deadlines); quirks flag in `keld.compat.ts` when per-app choice is legitimate and both branches have tests; ✘ when documented-never, substrate-blocked, or guard-denied — always with a `keld migrate` diagnostic naming the call site. Never silent, never `0%`/`100%`.

q2.position:
Measured advantage today is narrow and all diagnostic: a 484,864 B Windows host binary vs Electron's ~120 MB class; Windows main-process RSS 19,552–21,880 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (main process only); Bun bootstrapping the VS Code extension host 53.3% sooner to Initialized with 42.8% lower RSS (narrow PoC); kipc Bun↔Rust p99 ≈101 µs on Windows (1 session, not publication-eligible). Everything else — ≤300 ms paint, ≤90 MiB census, ≤20 MB installer, ≤50 KB patch, ≥1 GB/s bulk — is a target, and the one apples-to-apples first-paint diagnostic has Electron ahead (275 ms vs Keld 469 ms, Windows). So the honest statement of where the advantage comes from is structural: no bundled Chromium (bytes), one lean host process plus Bun instead of a Node-bearing main (host RSS, CPU), host-owned supervision (recovery), and purpose-built framing (latency floor). Rust per se buys none of it (arch 01 principle 4; reference §31).

Where compatibility *costs* performance — and these are costs Electron does not pay, so they must be measured before any 'faster than Electron' sentence: (1) Facade round trips: every Electron main-process API call that is an in-process C++ call in Electron (window getters, `webContents.send`, `Menu` updates) becomes a cross-process kipc CALL (~46 µs p50 diagnostic) or a mirror read; the mirror design in Q1 is exactly a performance mitigation and must be measured as such. (2) Renderer↔main messages take two hops and at least three copies on Keld (page→isolated world→host via WKScriptMessage JSON, host→Bun via kipc postcard, and the reverse), versus one Mojo hop in Electron; draw.io's `rendererReq`/`mainResp` protocol and Zettlr's 49 `webContents.send` sites plus 187 `invoke` sites are exactly this path. (3) Structured-clone codec: Electron's `any[]` with Date/Map/Set/ArrayBuffer/cycles must be encoded into a kipc-compatible codec and back; JSON is not sufficient and a faithful codec allocates — this conflicts with the no-steady-state-allocation rule unless it lives entirely on the Bun/renderer side with the host passing opaque bytes. (4) sendSync emulation (if implemented) blocks the renderer on a deadline-bounded host call. (5) Chatty event mirrors: pushing every window state change to keep sync getters honest is itself traffic.

Measure first, in this order, with the §5.1 census rules: (a) product cold start→first paint for draw.io-on-Keld vs draw.io-on-Electron 44.4.5: census = `keld-host` + guardian + Bun primary (the window exists only after authenticated HELLO), clock armed before host spawn to the `PAINT-OPPORTUNITY` beacon, `fresh-process` scored and `boot-cold` reported separately, median with bootstrap CI over 30 valid samples; a host-only `--hello` arm is a diagnostic, never the score. (b) Idle RSS 1 window: keld-owned processes only (host, guardian, Bun; WebKit XPCs excluded and reported as a separate coalition lane), condition-based stability, RSS as named counter with private footprint as mandatory companion; fresh-process vs warm-cache never pooled; >5% unexplained swing is INCONCLUSIVE. (c) New facade metric, not in §5: renderer `ipcRenderer.invoke` round trip through preload→host→Bun→back, 6-byte and 1,024-byte payloads, client-timed, ≥20 sessions × 100,000 calls, compared to the §5.1 kipc small-message row to attribute facade overhead separately from transport. (d) `webContents.send` fan-out rate at 1 KiB and the encode/decode cost of the structured-clone codec in isolation. (e) Installer size per delivered lane (`.dmg`), one sample + one reproducibility rebuild, decimal MB, including embedded Bun. Only after (a)–(e) exist as attributed JSON in keld-benches does the compat scoreboard get a 'facade overhead' column; the budget scoreboard and compat scoreboard remain separate ledgers.

Sequence (consume the spine, do not fork it): KEL-142 is Done and is the renderer/API seam; KEL-141 (prebuilt mac CLI) is the only spine item the proof truly needs next because 'config-only' is meaningless if the user must build Rust; KEL-140 (one guarded fs op) and KEL-143 (recovery) stay on the spine and are *not* gates for the activation cell — recovery is a later cell.
